newsitem.title: USA: Research Triangle Park, a zip code for high tech.
newsitem.headline: Research Triangle Park, a zip code for high tech.

text.p: Research Triangle Park is home to research and development operations for nearly 100 companies, but more than a thousand entrepreneurs seeking to cash in on the prestigious business address have post office boxes here.

Nestled in central North Carolina, Research Triangle Park has become a well-known home to the research operations of such corporate giants as International Business Machines Corp., Motorola Inc., Northern Telecom and Glaxo Wellcome, the U.S. arm of Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc.

But smaller telecommunications, computer and research companies -- often the spinoffs or start-ups of scientists who were let go in a merger or layoff -- receive mail each day at an address at the corporate campus bordered by three universities, a major research centre for some three decades.

"A Research Triangle Park address is instant credibility," said Andre Boisvert, chief executive of Alternate Realities Corp., a Raleigh, N.C.-based maker of virtual reality systems that uses the address. "It's the seal of approval for high-tech and research companies."
There are 99 research and development companies on the corporate campus, an official said. But nearly all 1,700 Post Office boxes at the Research Triangle Park post office are used by entrepreneurs.

"The boxes do turn over, but there is never a surplus. If a post office box becomes available, it is rented immediately because everyone wants to be associated with the Research Triangle Park," said Deborah Wiggins-Wooten, branch operations manager of the post office here.

To purchase land and erect a building in the park costs at least $360,000 for a minimum 8-acre (3.2-hectare) site, although office space can be leased at $17 a square foot, said Robin Smith, assistant treasurer and research manager for Research Triangle Foundation, which manages the campus.
On the other hand, a post office box in the coveted business locale costs $172 a year for the largest box.
The park was created in 1959 by the universities, government, and industry leaders to be an economic engine for the state.

It is a 6,800-acre (2720 hectares) campus bordered by the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill, Duke University in Durham and North Carolina State University in Raleigh, the state capital. It is in an unincorporated area, not subject to municipal taxes. No one lives in Research Triangle Park.
School faculty and administrators work closely with the companies in the park, whose laboratories are often a training ground for graduate students.

"The ultimate goal was to create jobs for the universities' graduates, many of whom left the state for employment when they finished school," according to Park Guide, a Research Triangle Park publication.

According to many accounts, the idea behind a research and development park caught on slowly until IBM decided to move in in the mid-1960s. Today it is a bedrock for research and development in the Southeast and beyond.
